coverage: Both parts and all 21 local chapters: principal participants, recalled family and social figures, imagined roles and named literary/historical allusions.

entities.name: The Underground Man
entities.body: The unnamed narrator: a retired civil servant living in Petersburg.

entities.name: Liza
entities.body: The young Russian woman from Riga working in the brothel the narrator visits.

entities.name: Apollon
entities.body: The narrator’s servant during his younger years, who also works as a tailor.

entities.name: Zverkov
entities.body: The narrator’s former schoolmate, now an army officer.

entities.name: Simonov
entities.body: The former schoolmate with whom the narrator still occasionally associates.

entities.name: Ferfitchkin
entities.body: The narrator’s former schoolmate and an admirer of Zverkov.

entities.name: Trudolyubov
entities.body: The army officer among the former schoolmates, a distant relation of Zverkov.

entities.name: Anton Antonitch Syetotchkin
entities.body: The narrator’s superior at the office and occasional social host.

entities.name: The officer at the government office
entities.body: The officer whose clanking sword irritates the narrator during his government service.

entities.name: The officer from the tavern
entities.body: The tall officer the narrator encounters at the billiard table and on Nevsky Prospect.

entities.name: The narrator’s later servant
entities.body: The older country woman employed by the narrator when he writes his notes.

entities.name: The brothel’s madam
entities.body: The woman running the brothel where Liza and Olympia work.

entities.name: Olympia
entities.body: A woman at the brothel, known to Zverkov and the narrator.

entities.name: The sledge-driver
entities.body: The driver hired by the narrator after the dinner.

entities.name: The restaurant waiters
entities.body: The staff serving the farewell dinner at the Hôtel de Paris.

entities.name: The narrator’s benefactor
entities.body: The distant relative whose inheritance allows the narrator to retire.

entities.name: The narrator’s childhood relations
entities.body: The relatives responsible for sending the narrator to school.

entities.name: The narrator’s school friend
entities.body: The unnamed boy whom the narrator recalls befriending at school.

entities.name: The other clerk
entities.body: The office colleague whose appearance the young narrator compares with his own.

entities.name: The clerk in the dirty uniform
entities.body: The second office colleague described by the young narrator, remembered for his old uniform.

entities.name: The wine connoisseur
entities.body: The narrator’s acquaintance who prides himself on his knowledge of Lafitte wine.

entities.name: The man thrown from the tavern
entities.body: The man the narrator sees thrown out during a fight with billiard cues.

entities.name: The officer’s porter
entities.body: The porter who gives the narrator information about the tall officer’s lodgings.

entities.name: The narrator’s patron
entities.body: The influential person who recommended the narrator for his job.

entities.name: The countess
entities.body: The unnamed aristocratic woman whom the narrator imagines among Nevsky Prospect’s fashionable public.

entities.name: Prince D.
entities.body: The aristocrat mentioned among the fashionable people on Nevsky Prospect.

entities.name: Anton Antonitch’s daughters
entities.body: The two teenage daughters in Anton Antonitch’s household.

entities.name: The daughters’ aunt
entities.body: The aunt who pours tea at Anton Antonitch’s gatherings.

entities.name: Anton Antonitch’s visitors
entities.body: The officials who gather to discuss work, pay and promotion at Anton Antonitch’s home.

entities.name: His Excellency
entities.body: The senior official discussed by Anton Antonitch’s visitors.

entities.name: The elderly general
entities.body: The father of the young women whom Zverkov approaches at the theater.

entities.name: The general’s daughters
entities.body: The young women whom Zverkov approaches at the theater.

entities.name: Prince Kolya
entities.body: The wealthy hussar whom Zverkov describes as his friend.

entities.name: The woman in Zverkov’s story
entities.body: The unnamed woman whose affection Zverkov boasts of winning.

entities.name: Podharzhevsky
entities.body: The hussar whose large income the dinner guests discuss.

entities.name: Princess D.
entities.body: The princess whose beauty the dinner guests discuss without having met her.

entities.name: Liza’s parents
entities.body: The tradespeople in Riga with whom Liza grew up.

entities.name: The woman in the coffin
entities.body: The dead woman described by the narrator in his story to Liza.

entities.name: The other madam
entities.body: The brothel keeper in the narrator’s account of the dead woman’s debts.

entities.name: The affectionate father
entities.body: The father whose devotion to his daughter the narrator describes to Liza.

entities.name: The affectionate father’s daughter
entities.body: The daughter in the narrator’s example of paternal devotion.

entities.name: The woman with the salt fish
entities.body: The woman the narrator describes seeing outside a brothel on New Year’s Day.

entities.name: Liza’s correspondent
entities.body: The young man from Riga whose affectionate letter Liza keeps; the narrator thinks he is a medical student.

entities.name: Liza’s friend
entities.body: The friend who accompanies Liza to a dance and passes on the young man’s letter.

entities.name: The hosts of the dance
entities.body: The family at whose house Liza meets her childhood acquaintance again.

entities.name: Vanuha
entities.body: The gravedigger named in the narrator’s imagined burial scene.

entities.name: Fyodor Dostoevsky
entities.body: The author of the novella, distinct from the fictional writer of the notes.

entities.name: The Wagenheims
entities.body: The Petersburg dentists whose name the narrator invokes in his discussion of toothache.

entities.name: Nikolai Ge
entities.body: The Russian painter whose surname this translation renders as Gay.

entities.name: Mikhail Saltykov-Shchedrin
entities.body: The Russian satirist alluded to as the author of As You Will.

entities.name: Henry Thomas Buckle
entities.body: The English historian cited for his theory of civilization and violence.

entities.name: Napoleon I
entities.body: The French emperor referred to as Napoleon the Great.

entities.name: Napoleon III
entities.body: The later French emperor, called the present Napoleon in the narrator’s historical comparison.

entities.name: Attila
entities.body: The ruler of the Huns, invoked as an example of a violent conqueror.

entities.name: Stenka Razin
entities.body: The Cossack leader of a major rebellion in seventeenth-century Russia.

entities.name: Cleopatra
entities.body: The Egyptian queen cited in the narrator’s account of cruelty in history.

entities.name: Anaevsky
entities.body: The Russian writer mockingly cited on the Colossus of Rhodes.

entities.name: The Colossus of Rhodes
entities.body: The ancient giant statue at Rhodes mentioned in the narrator’s historical digression.

entities.name: Heinrich Heine
entities.body: The German poet cited on the difficulty of writing a truthful autobiography.

entities.name: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
entities.body: The author of the Confessions, discussed as an example of autobiographical self-presentation.

entities.name: Nikolai Nekrasov
entities.body: The Russian poet whose verse introduces the second part.

entities.name: Juliet Soskice
entities.body: The translator credited for the poem introducing the second part.

entities.name: Kostanzhoglo
entities.body: The efficient landowner in Gogol’s Dead Souls, invoked as a practical ideal.

entities.name: Uncle Pyotr Ivanitch
entities.body: The pragmatic uncle in Goncharov’s A Common Story, invoked as a model of worldly success.

entities.name: The imagined King of Spain
entities.body: The royal identity used as an example of delusion, recalling Gogol’s Diary of a Madman.

entities.name: Nikolai Gogol
entities.body: The Russian writer whose comic officer Pirogov is recalled.

entities.name: Lieutenant Pirogov
entities.body: The officer in Gogol’s Nevsky Prospect used as a comparison for the narrator’s adversary.

entities.name: Tchurkin
entities.body: The shopkeeper whose establishment supplies the narrator’s gloves and hat.

entities.name: Manfred
entities.body: Byron’s tormented dramatic hero, invoked as a model for the narrator’s fantasies.

entities.name: The pope
entities.body: The head of the Catholic Church as a figure in the narrator’s fantasy.

entities.name: William Shakespeare
entities.body: The English playwright whose lasting fame the dinner guests discuss.

entities.name: Alexander Pushkin
entities.body: The Russian writer whose fictional duelist Silvio supplies a model for the narrator’s fantasy.

entities.name: Silvio
entities.body: The duelist in Pushkin’s The Shot, recalled during the narrator’s revenge fantasy.

entities.name: Mikhail Lermontov
entities.body: The Russian writer of Masquerade, mentioned as another source of the narrator’s fantasy.

entities.name: Lovelace
entities.body: The seducer in Richardson’s Clarissa, used as a comparison in the narrator’s description of Zverkov.

entities.name: George Sand
entities.body: The French novelist invoked as a model for the narrator’s sentimental imaginings.

entities.name: Alexander the Great
entities.body: The Macedonian conqueror invoked in the narrator’s comparison of Apollon’s vanity.

entities.name: God
entities.body: The deity invoked in the narrator’s prayers, exclamations and moral language.

entities.name: The devil
entities.body: The supernatural figure invoked in the narrator’s exclamations.
